chapter_note: Despite the synopsis’s ‘composite’ character, most paragraphs preserve an older cosmological time-measure teaching: emanation durations are expressed by internal cosmic imagery (storehouses, aeons, borders, descent/ascent, Last Statue, chaining). A later editorial/meta-teaching layer appears where the text pivots to what ‘apostles/teachers/chosen’ can or cannot proclaim about the two eternities; these paragraphs are treated as non-core. Several paragraphs are MIXED where brief audience-address or transmission talk (‘listen’, ‘I recounted to you’, ‘disciples’) introduces otherwise core cosmological exposition.

paragraphs.core_text: [...] a great ju[d/ge ...] now also a ti[me ...] that they sculpt[ed ...] he was revealed in the Father, the first established thing.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Lacunosely formulates a primordial ‘first established thing’ revealed in the Father; no citation or institutional/application hook is visible.

paragraphs.core_text: W[he]n [...] the two summonses that he called [...] the Mother of Life [...] a long duration in the first Father [...]
paragraphs.temporal_note: Emanation/‘summons’ language in a purely cosmological register (Mother of Life, first Father, duration).

paragraphs.core_text: For someone, if he might set a measure and rule [...] the earth {particles} and the {pebbles} of the mountains and [...] of the sea and the body of the firmaments. Should they be poured [...] the body of the four mountains and the three vessels that surround the universe; if they shall all be poured out [...] these fine {granules}.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Old ‘measurement’ analogy: cosmic architecture (firmaments, four mountains, three vessels) used to express immeasurable duration—cosmos→cosmos mapping.

paragraphs.core_text: Happen you know that the grains of the earth {particles} are measurable, [and those of] the [entire] universe. It is possible to count the {particles} of the earth each year [...] the sand grains of the entire universe; but the duration of the time that the Great Spirit spent in the Father, [the] first established thing, one will not be able to make a count of it!
paragraphs.temporal_note: Contrasts measurable created quantities with uncountable divine duration; Great Spirit ‘in the Father’ is internal cosmological exposition.

paragraphs.core_text: He first sculpted her like this. He established her in his inner storehouses in quiet and silence. When [they had] need of her she was called and came forth of the Father [of Greatness]. She looked at all her aeons of light!
paragraphs.temporal_note: Pure emanation mechanics (sculpted/established/called; storehouses; aeons of light). No institutional pointing.

paragraphs.core_text: Once again, from the time when she was called to [...] go to [...] she gave [...] upon his [bod]y [...] all the aeons [...]; she also [...] all of them. This [is also the case] with the First Man.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Continues the emanation-duration schema and parallels it with the First Man; still internal cosmological description.

paragraphs.core_text: This is how the Man spent a long time being anointed in the Mother, set fast in her inner storehouses [...]; the extent of time—from when the First Man went down to the contest, till the time when the [Statue (?) co]mes i[n ...] this time [...] he appeared [...]
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed brief audience-address/transmission tag: “that I have recounted to you—” (speaker-to-audience intrusion into an otherwise impersonal duration schema).
paragraphs.temporal_note: Core temporal span is given by descent/ascent markers (contest; Last Statue), but a first-person delivery aside suggests later compilation voice.

paragraphs.core_text: Again, from when he was called and came forth, till the time when he [himse]lf called the five shining [gods] who are his sons; they themselves also spent a long time existing in their father! It is the time that occurred from the coming down of the First Man till the going up of the Last Statue. The five gods spent this much duration being anointed in the First Man. Yet, [at the] time when they were awaited, they were called and came forth.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Systematic, internally bounded timing of emanation (father→sons; anointing; descent/ascent; Last Statue) with no external application.

paragraphs.core_text: At the time when the Mother of Life was called from the Father of Greatness, when she expelled herself and came down by her own wish, from the heights of the Father to the earth, [she would spend thousands of] years and many ten thousands until she reached the earth. [Fo]r there is no measure nor rule to the heights of the Father. Rather, [just as] he had called her in his Great Spirit, so he set her upon [the] land of greatness through one of these three that are counted to the twelve hidden ones within the light veil, the ones [esta]blished after the [...] region of the south.
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed opening exhortation/teaching-address: “Listen also to this, how I would teach you it.”
paragraphs.temporal_note: Core is a highly systematized cosmological timing/topography (twelve hidden ones; light veil; south region). The ‘listen/how I teach’ is later delivery framing.

paragraphs.core_text: [The] matter of the Mother [of L]ife is like this. When [the Father called her he established her in the place he pleased,] and she examined everywhere that [...] a blink of an eye, or like a [...] bird [...]
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed outward-pointing institutional/application phrase: “to establish her there as the instruction of the people that [...] many [...]” (cosmos→‘people’ application).
paragraphs.temporal_note: Core describes instantaneous perception/agency of the Mother of Life (blink of an eye / bird simile), but an inserted ‘instruction of the people’ clause shifts to contemporary-aimed didactic purpose.

paragraphs.core_text: This also is lik[e ... the] Mother of Life in [...] whenever [...] cast her out [...] upon her to the place [...] him. He perfected her in his Great Spirit and set her in [the place he pl]eased, according to [his will].
paragraphs.temporal_note: Emanation ‘perfected/set’ within Great Spirit; purely internal divine action language.

paragraphs.core_text: [Th]is [also is how] they called the [five g]ods from the [Fi]rst Man. They were set before him, as he wished that [...]-ness [...] down, that they would rule in them [...] one another. He ordered and distributed them [...] the son. He stripped himself of them [...] and he [...] he girt and bound himself to [...] in a [...] of silence upon the border of the earth [...]
paragraphs.temporal_note: Old systematic ‘calling/ordering/distributing’ of the five gods; border-of-earth motif stays within cosmic architecture.

paragraphs.core_text: Again, he too, the First Man, spent a long period and [time] until he gave power to his sons; until he assu[m]ed them. After he came to wear them he stood fast in the heights between the borders. Again, he spent a duration and time like this, corresponding to such amount and measure as the raindrops and dew and falls of mist that come down in the universe. This is how he spent this duration also, standing between the borders, until the hour when he cast himself down to the contest!
paragraphs.temporal_note: Characteristic substrate ‘measure-by-cosmos’ similes (raindrops/dew/mist) and degree-like staging (between the borders → contest).

paragraphs.core_text: Whenever the Father of Greatn[e]ss called the Great Spirit and the First Man and the gods of the glorious one, who are provided to enable them to reveal him; at that very time [he] sculpted the Great Builder in the [land of] light, [and] the Living Spirit with the mighty and active gods who came [from] him. Also, at that time, he sculpted the [Amb]assador, with Jesus the Splendour and the Virgin of Light and the Pillar of Glory, and the gods who came from them. [All these the Father of Greatness sculpted at] a single time. They came forth of one another, one after one; the time when [...] and the work.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Systematic emanation catalogue in a fully internal cosmological hierarchy (including Jesus the Splendour as a cosmic being, not a Gospel citation).

paragraphs.core_text: from the time when the Darkness raised itself up to [...] essence of the light [...] these three emanations [...] from the will of the Father against the enemy [...] he has [...] Darkness [...] according to the will [...] the universe [...] in it [...] separate out [...] rest him in which way, and he rejoices [...] in his kingdom; until [the time when the face] of the Father will be unveiled over [all] the gods of glory, and all the rich ones of [...] the em[anations] who came forth against the enemy.
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed speaker-to-audience transmission fragment: “[...] to recount it to you [...]”.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Core contrasts Light vs Darkness and frames history between uprising and final unveiling—cosmic timeline; the ‘recount to you’ is later delivery voice.

paragraphs.core_text: [From] that time when he sculpted these three [...] till the time when the Father would unveil his face, [and they] go in to his hidden storehouses, and he calls them [...] establishes each one of them to his place. There is no measure nor rule to this period until that time.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Impersonal temporal measurelessness plus storehouse/placing mechanics: classic structural cosmology.
Meta-discourse about ‘teachers/saviours/apostles of greatness’ and what they can proclaim; institutional transmission register rather than cosmological exposition.
Continues institutional ‘apostles and teachers’ limitation language; focuses on proclamation rather than describing cosmic mechanisms.
Fragmentary question-form about an ‘eternal end’ suggests an editorial/Q-style transition rather than core exposition.

paragraphs.core_text: about this Matter, this thought of death [...] ; for [this] is the way that [...] came up to its storehouses. It has [...] in its five elements.
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed question/answer transmission scaffolding referring to a speaker and ‘disciples’ (“However, [...] to enable him to recoun[t ...] who asks him [...] of the disciples [...] because [...] and he gives [...]”). Also removed “which I have told you”.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Core resumes internal evil-process mechanics (Matter; storehouses; five elements). The surrounding ‘who asks / disciples / I told you’ is later delivery framing.

paragraphs.core_text: Again, it also [...] the period and the time that it spent, until it revealed itself to its elements, before it came to the trees. It spent a great period and a long time established [...] before it came up to the trees. It was [...] in the trees. It spent a long time and duration [...] existing in them, before it sculpted the fru[its ...] and sculpted the fruits.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Evil emanation staged through elements → trees → fruits; entirely within the cosmological process register.

paragraphs.core_text: Again, it spent a long [time] in the fruits. Not little is the period and the time that it spent existing in the fruits, before it sculpted [...] after a long time [...] the d[emon]s of its five worlds in various forms [can not (?) ] be measured [...] in p[erfec]tion of the fruits in the demons and fiends. They fell upon their earth and [...] were nourished. Not little is the period that they [spent in the wo]rlds, until they were nourished amongst [...] to make [...] that land which shines, and the great [King] who dwells there.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Highly characteristic internal cosmology: five worlds; demons/fiends; nourishment; emergence of a shining land and its King (cosmos→cosmos).

paragraphs.core_text: [You] know that [...] that in [...] at the time when he [...] its essence. It assumed [...] Matter [...] to the war [...] the Perfect Man. [From the time] when the war occurred [...]
paragraphs.temporal_note: Though lacunose, it stays inside the mythic-cosmological conflict schema (Matter vs Perfect Man), not institutional application.

paragraphs.core_text: [The first is ...] he came to be in some [...] when they ensnared a [...]
paragraphs.temporal_note: Begins a numbered/list structure about cosmic history; despite damage, it reads as internal cosmological sequencing.

paragraphs.core_text: [The second is ...] that he built [...] the universe was established. The zone [...] down until the time when it will be dissolved.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Internal cosmogonic stage (‘built’; universe established; dissolution horizon).

paragraphs.core_text: The third is the [...] the things and the universe will [...] from the time when they were established there, till the time when their end will be complete and their existence ceases [...]
paragraphs.temporal_note: Temporal span of created existence framed cosmologically (established → end complete).

paragraphs.core_text: [The fourth is the dissolution when they will dissolve the universe] there, and all things are destroyed. Obliteration reaches them in that great fire, [which will] burn them for fourteen hundred and sixty-eight years.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Eschatological ‘great fire’ within the system; the specific year-count may reflect later calculation, but it remains internal to cosmic process (no institutional mapping).

paragraphs.core_text: [The fift]h is the way that the Last Statue will be sculpted [from] the remnant of all things. The light separates out to its place, and goes up and rules in its kingdom. However, [the da]rkness [...] and they take it in to the tomb [...] and they are bound with it in an eternal chain.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Classic Manichaean end-process: Last Statue; separation; Light enthronement; Darkness chained—fully cosmological.

paragraphs.core_text: Now, from [the tim]e when this first war occurred, till the time of this chain [...] these five things [...] light.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Summarizing temporal bracket (war → chain) for the preceding five items; remains an internal cosmic chronology.

paragraphs.core_text: However, before [...] from it out of the powers [...] and measure it; because it is eternal.
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed institutional ‘revelation competence’ clause: “it is possible for the apostles and the chosen and the teachers to speak and recount about it.”
paragraphs.temporal_note: Core remnant asserts an eternal, immeasurable pre-stage; the excised clause applies the teaching to church roles (‘apostles/chosen/teachers’), indicating later editorial reflection.
Fragment continues the meta-epistemic limitation theme (‘No person is able ...’), not advancing cosmological correspondences/mechanics.
Explicit institutional roles (‘the apostle and the teacher’) in a statement about what can be spoken; late frame/meta layer, not substrate exposition.
